```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "Feasibility within 90 days favors A. Its core build is polling a directory, checking against a schedule, validating shape and alerting. The brief describes this as low-complexity, which suits one person running AI agents. B's stated differentiator, filing the country-of-residence return as well, means liability-bearing tax logic across multiple jurisdictions. The brief itself says this is materially larger than anything existing competitors chose to tackle.",
    "B has heavy setup work that sits on the critical path to a first sale. It needs IRS EFIN authorization with a suitability check and annual IRS software acceptance testing. Its own open questions say the timeline is unknown. It also needs GDPR counsel review before launch. A's regulatory burden is lighter. A BAA or DPA applies only to some customers, and the brief marks SOC 2 as a later concern.",
    "Both ideas show budget exists, but A's payer can buy in any month. B's payer pays once per filing season, which may not fall inside a 90-day window. A's anchors are sourced: Files.com bundles an equivalent feature at $199/mo, and Nodinite cites $3,600/yr.",
    "If B drops the local-country filing, it falls back to a US-only market with six self-serve competitors at commoditized prices of $67-$219. A's weaknesses are real: bundling by Files.com and teams building the poller themselves. Still, they leave a clear segment to test quickly: teams on bare SFTP with no MFT platform who are too busy to script a monitor.",
    "B does have stronger and more recent demand quotes, including Reddit users quoted $800-$2,500 by accountants. A's quotes are from 2012 and 2016, and its third item is an unverified seed reference. This narrows the gap but does not outweigh B's scope and regulatory risk for a 90-day first-customer goal."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B's case for rests on the claim that Atamatax, built solo, 'can charge $199-$799 and attract customers.' The only source cited is Atamatax's own pricing and marketing site. No customer count, revenue or traction evidence is given. It shows a listed price, not proof that customers pay it, yet the brief uses it to validate the whole one-person build model.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate. B has better demand evidence, while A's demand quotes are old and thin. A's own case against, a bundled feature that teams can build in an afternoon with cron and Slack, could sink it. The pick rests mainly on B's scope, regulatory gating and seasonality, which make a paying customer within 90 days much less likely, not on A being strongly validated."
}
```
